# Incident Report — MTA 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence reviewed
- `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 packets, 4.6 MB). No separate IDS/Suricata export was present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived entirely from packet analysis with `tshark`.

## Victim host
| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **192.168.1.216** | Source of all suspect traffic; sole non-DC/non-router host generating outbound connections |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** | ARP table (`192.168.1.216 -> 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`) and DHCP `chaddr`, consistent across the capture |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP `Option 12 Host Name` and Kerberos `CNameString` (`DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$`, machine account) agree. NBNS name-service broadcasts from the same IP show `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2` (one-character NetBIOS discrepancy) — DHCP + Kerberos agreement is treated as authoritative. |
| Logged-in domain user | **steve.smith** (domain `SPOONWATCH.NET`, workgroup name `SPOONWATCH`) | Kerberos `AS-REQ`/`TGS-REQ` `CNameString` frames 829/839 |

Domain controller for context: `SPOONWATCH-DC` at 192.168.1.2 (NBNS/Kerberos/LDAP/CLDAP traffic, all internal AD chatter — benign).

## Malware family
**Vidar-class information stealer** — **behavioral attribution** (no binary was recovered from the capture and no explicit family string/YARA/signature match was made; the call is based on the exfiltration protocol, log-archive structure, and header fingerprint, all of which are strong, well-known TTPs for this family).

Grounds for the call:
- Single sustained HTTP (not HTTPS) connection, `192.168.1.216:49738 -> 2.56.57.108:80`, TCP stream 65, contacted by **bare IP with no preceding DNS lookup** (no query for 2.56.57.108 appears anywhere in the DNS traffic — hardcoded/fallback C2 IP).
- Fixed, distinctive request header block on every POST, with **no `User-Agent`** and Russian-locale headers on a self-generated HTTP client (not a real browser):
  `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, application/xhtml+xml, image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/x-xbitmap, */*;q=0.1`
  `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`
  `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16, *;q=0.1`
- Data exfiltrated as a single multipart/form-data POST to `/osk/` (frame 4816, `Content-Length: 379629`) with field `name="file"; filename="_5861695120.zip"` — carved and validated as a real ZIP (`PK\x03\x04`, central directory intact, compression=deflate).
- The archive's internal structure is the signature Vidar stealer-log layout:
  ```
  autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt   autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
  cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt         cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
  cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt    cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt
  outlook.txt   passwords.txt   screenshot.jpg   system.txt
  ```
  (per-browser-profile autofill/cookie/CC folders + passwords/system-info/Outlook/screenshot files, timestamped 2022-01-07 20:07 inside the zip) — this exact folder taxonomy and the `_<numeric HWID>.zip` naming convention are hallmark Vidar behavior, not seen in RedLine/Raccoon-style flat logs.
- Preceded and followed by seven small "beacon" POSTs to `/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` and `/osk//main.php`, each with `Content-Length: 25` and a body that is only the closing multipart boundary — check-in/heartbeat traffic to the same PHP gate, receiving `HTTP/200` acks (some with a benign, unrelated 200-byte image body from the server, others 0-length).

No delivery/dropper stage (initial infection vector) is visible in this capture — only the post-compromise exfiltration phase was captured.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP) — sole C2 channel, contacted directly by IP (evidence: tcp.stream 65, frames 1501–4830)

**URLs**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — exfil gate, received the stolen-data ZIP (frame 4816)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — beacon endpoint (frame 4275)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `http://2.56.57.108/osk//7.jpg` — beacon endpoints (frames 1501, 1641, 2225, 2541, 2691, 3054, 4194)

**Domains**
- None. The C2 was contacted by bare IPv4 address only; no DNS resolution for it appears in the capture.

**File names**
- `_5861695120.zip` — multipart filename of the exfiltrated stealer-log archive (frame 4816 `Content-Disposition` header)
- Contents of that archive (all timestamped 2022-01-07 20:07): `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`

**File hashes (SHA256)**
- `231a19c496ad42a6755f1afe8c79d5b376d9a1f204e96d990acddaa6ca866292` — carved ZIP payload (`_5861695120.zip`, the exact multipart body bytes as transmitted in frame 4816). Note: a handful of internal entries fail full inflate/CRC verification, consistent with minor TCP-stream reassembly noise in the capture rather than any evidence issue with the identification above (the ZIP central directory, file names, and sizes are intact and reliable).
- No executable/DLL payload was transferred to or from the C2 in this capture, so there is no dropper-binary hash to report.

## Benign context (ruled out, not IOCs)
Every other external conversation from 192.168.1.216 is legitimate Microsoft/Windows infrastructure, confirmed by TLS SNI / plaintext HTTP Host and Microsoft user-agent strings:
`download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.225/.201, 8.253.189.126 — Windows Update, incl. legitimate signed `.cab` updates and the Defender `am_delta_patch...exe` delta definition update), `fe2cr.update.microsoft.com` (52.249.36.204), `fe3cr.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` (20.54.89.15), `cp801.prod.do.dsp.mp.microsoft.com` / `kv801...` (184.50.62.43), `pti.store.microsoft.com` (104.212.67.47), `v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com` (20.189.173.1, 52.178.17.2, 20.50.80.210), `geo.prod.do.dsp.mp.microsoft.com` (52.179.216.235), `self.events.data.microsoft.com` (52.168.112.67), `settings-win.data.microsoft.com` (52.183.220.149), `client.wns.windows.com` (40.83.240.146), `www.bing.com` / `api.msn.com` (204.79.197.200/.203). All internal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/CLDAP/NBNS/DHCP traffic to 192.168.1.1/.2 is normal domain-joined workstation activity.

## Incident summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user **steve.smith** on `SPOONWATCH.NET`, was infected with a **Vidar-class information stealer** (behavioral attribution). The malware harvested Chrome/Edge autofill data, cookies, saved credit-card fields, saved passwords, Outlook data, a desktop screenshot, and system information, packaged them into `_5861695120.zip`, and exfiltrated the archive via a single plaintext HTTP POST to a hardcoded C2 at `2.56.57.108:80/osk/`, bracketed by heartbeat check-ins to sibling `/osk//*.jpg` and `/osk//main.php` paths on the same host. No delivery/dropper stage is present in this capture, only the post-compromise data-theft phase.
